# Frozen M3 migration fixture

`m3-schema2.sqlite3.gz` was generated by the actual code at frozen commit
`68643756ea1b36f9c8ba1cf87196d6f04b080245`, not by the M4 encoder.
It contains `build_street_world(seed=71).world` after the idempotent
`frozen-m3-move` command starts the merchant's journey to `royal-exchange`.
The old `save_snapshot` writes schema 2; gzip uses `-n` for deterministic headers.
No private saved-game data is included.

To reproduce, extract `git archive` of that commit into a temporary directory
and run Python with that directory first on `sys.path`:

```python
world = build_street_world(seed=71).world
execute_once(world, 'frozen-m3-move', move, world, 'merchant', 'royal-exchange')
save_snapshot(world, temporary_sqlite_path)
```

The frozen encoder's SHA-256 of `_payload_for(world)` is
`18de2acac2c18c2376d8b494765a47a4a0c00f289e9a01f4577cc66d40384ff8`.
After 24 calls to `advance_world(world, 1)`, it is
`fe510d1a807fc7789c7521395b64969a35c89c416e1c40ad9ffda3fc598356a3`
with 964 events at `1770-01-02T00:00:00`.
The migration test removes only the three new empty registries and projects
the document header back to schema 2 before comparison. Its digest covers all
original canonical state, runtime data, command ledger, active movements,
RNG state, event IDs, inventory, finance and transport, not just event counts.
